newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas extends gains on outages, SW heat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas extends gains on outages, SW heat.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices extended their gains Wednesday as buyers continued to flood the market amid an unexpected nuclear outage and warmer-than-normal weather in the Southwest, sources said.
Louisiana Gulf prices at the Henry Hub gained another nine to 10 cents to about $2.31-2.35 per mmBtu, mirroring the rising June Henry Hub futures contract in the $2.30s.

Entergy Corp's 936 megawatt River Bend nuclear unit in Louisiana tripped off line Tuesday due to problems with a flow control valve in the reactor circulation system. The company said the unit would likely be down for one to two weeks.
This outage followed Tuesday's news that Texas Utilities' 1,150 MW Comanche Peak 2 nuclear unit was reduced to 46 percent power for repairs. The unit began increasing power this morning.
Also, Entergy Corp's 858 MW Arkansas 2 nuclear unit is operating at 75 percent power for testing.
The inflated Gulf prices coupled with cooler forecasts boosted New York city-gate prices by about five to 10 cents to the high-$2.50s to low-$2.60s.
Appalachian prices were up a similar amount to the low-to-mid $2.50s on Columbia and CNG.
In the Midcontinent, where most temperatures remained below normal, prices firmed by an average of 10 cents to about $2.10-2.15.
Demarcation was quoted mostly around $2.13-2.15, also up about 10 cents from Tuesday.
Chicago city-gate values also jumped 10 cents to the low-to-mid $2.40s, while Detroit city-gate gas sold at $2.47-2.50.
Temperatures are expected to drop well below normal on Friday throughout most of the upper Midwest.
In west Texas, Permian prices were also up 10 cents to $2.04-2.11, while prices at the southern California border climbed into low-to-mid $2.20s.
Estimates for tonight's American Gas Association ranged mostly from 40-50 bcf of injections, versus a gain of 53 bcf a year ago.
